newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat steady in quiet Australian market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat steady in quiet Australian market.

text.p: Australian wheat futures traded quietly on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Wednesday with just seven trades in July 1997 the only activity.
The contract rose by 50 cents to A$170.00 on the trade.
Settlement prices for the nearer-term contracts came back generally by about A$2.00 a tonne, while more distant contracts failed to attract interest.

Kerrin Gleeson, of Elders Risk Management, said the quiet market reflected the ending of harvest concerns for growers. News of the higher Australian pool price and good export contracts had been absorbed by the market, she said.
Other traders pointed out that Chicago's focus on Australian wheat had been dominated by the announcement of a record 23.0 million tonnes crop by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB).
However, the AWB also said in its Monday announcement that it estimated Australia would export close to 17.0 million tonnes of wheat this year.
This was a significant advance on the current USDA estimate for Australian exports of 13.5 million tonnes, they said.
